reasons: reasoning continuity is tool-loop fragile: WS-13 §8.2 records a hard 400 when reasoning state is missing mid-tool-loop, and the Anthropic dialect's own continuity contract for this vendor is unproven — the tool-loop corpus must pass before promotion

continuationDomain.sourceRef: BOTH halves. Own-state acceptance: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/anthropic_api (read 2026-10-29): the compatibility table lists assistant content `type = "thinking"` as Supported (and `redacted_thinking` as Not Supported). The Anthropic adapter replays the model's own thinking blocks on its next request. Whether omission errors in a tool loop is not documented for this dialect (the OpenAI-format 400 is DeepSeek's `reasoning_content` rule, not this one). Why the domain is NARROW: the state is valid only for the model that produced it on this route -- a different model, or the same model at another provider (a different credential and account), never receives it, and the history renderer strips it there.

pricing.sourceRef: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/ (retrieved 2026-09-19) — DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash PEAK rate per 1M tokens: cache-miss input $0.30, cache-hit input $0.006, output $1.20. The page also publishes lower off-peak rates ($0.15 / $0.003 / $0.60), which `ModelPricing` cannot represent. Peak is intentionally recorded so budget estimates do not under-report during peak hours; it over-reports off-peak usage.
